title: Add incremental RAG 'watchmode' authoring quickstart with dev inspector
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: speed up authoring loop for retrieval-augmented generation workflows by providing a tiny local-first quickstart that watches content, incrementally updates an embeddings index, exposes a web-based inspector for request/response traces and index diffing, and includes a small tool-calling agent sample that demonstrates structured output and fallback routing. What this PR adds: 1) a new quickstart under quickstarts/rag-watchmode that contains a lightweight Node CLI (watchmode) which monitors a user-specified content folder, computes incremental embeddings checkpoints, and writes compact shard deltas to ./index-shards. 2) a small Python agent example that uses the incremental index and demonstrates tool-binding for a web-search stub and a citation formatter. 3) a local dev inspector (single-file Express + static UI) served on http://localhost:8081 that visualizes recent queries, nearest-neighbor results, and tokenized prompt diffs to aid prompt iteration. 4) docs site updates: new quickstart guide, sidebar entry, and a short troubleshooting section covering common watchmode pitfalls and KMS key hints for private deployments. 5) lightweight telemetry probes and CI smoke tests that exercise the watch loop and inspector startup. Checklist: - [x] scaffold quickstart files and templates - [x] implement watchmode CLI with incremental embedding checkpointing - [x] provide Python agent sample and minimal TS client shim - [x] add dev inspector and README walkthrough - [x] add docs site page and sidebar registration - [x] add CI smoke test and linting - [x] run local manual validation and fix flakiness Notable implementation details: The CLI uses a content hashing strategy to avoid re-embedding unchanged files and writes per-namespace shard manifests to allow safe interruption and resume. Embedding generation is decoupled so teams can swap the Redwood-API call with a local embedder binary for on-prem usage. The inspector is intentionally minimal to avoid adding a heavy dependency; it reads the same shard deltas that the CLI produces and renders a compact timeline. Compatibility notes: works with both hosted Redwood API and private deployments; for private installs, pass REDWOOD_API_URL and REDWOOD_API_KEY. No breaking API changes. How to try locally: git clone, cd quickstarts/rag-watchmode, npm install, pip install -r requirements.txt, start CLI with node bin/watchmode.js --content ./examples/content --inspect, open http://localhost:8081, run sample agent with python samples/sample_agent.py. Testing: added a CI job quickstart-watch-smoke that runs the CLI against a small corpus and verifies index shard creation and inspector health endpoint. Security/privacy: default quickstart ships with a sample content set not containing any PII. For customer data, docs include KMS/HSM notes and a checklist for scrubbing sensitive fields before indexing. Migration/rollout: this is a new quickstart and opt-in for users. Related work: complements ENG-3742 (incremental indexing RFC) and DOC-811 (quickstart site reorg).

release_notes: Added 'Incremental RAG Watchmode' quickstart: a local-first authoring workflow with an incremental embedding CLI, dev inspector UI, and a sample tool-calling agent. Designed for fast prompt-index cycles and safe incremental updates. No breaking changes.
notes_for_support: If users report missing shards or duplicate embeddings, ask for the output of watchmode --status and the generated shard-manifest.json. For private installs confirm REDWOOD_API_URL and credentials are set. For firewall issues with the inspector suggest using --inspect-port and confirm local host binding.
acceptance_criteria: - Quickstart CLI starts and writes index shards using the fixture corpus within CI timeout. - Inspector serves /health and shows at least one query in the timeline when sample agent runs. - Docs page renders in the site preview and sidebar link is present.
manual_test_steps: 1) Clone repo and cd quickstarts/rag-watchmode 2) npm ci && pip install -r requirements.txt 3) node bin/watchmode.js --content ./examples/content --inspect --inspect-port 8081 4) open http://localhost:8081 and confirm inspector loads 5) python python/samples/sample_agent.py --index ./index-shards --query 'Who is the CEO?' 6) verify CI smoke job output in .github/workflows/quickstart-watch-smoke logs
